leverage.exposure: No leveraged position, and none opens if the live bid lands — the commitment sits comfortably inside available cash and leaves positive headroom. That is the entire reason no second bid is permitted: every remaining asset on the board costs more than the headroom that would be left, so adding one would push the balance negative and zero out the whole matchday. Spending remains capped by the floor rather than by cash, and the floor is not close to binding at current commitments.

binding_gap: Attack, and behind it midfield depth. The squad is defender-heavy and defence caps out in every legal shape, so a sixth defender cannot improve the eleven unless he is good enough to displace the weakest one — and that argument only ever worked for a player with a known scoring history and a dated starter guarantee. Both new defenders on the board this run fail that test. The gap is a third attacker, which is exactly what the live bid buys.

verdict.headline: No action.
verdict.detail: No action. The Gomis raise is placed, live and unopposed, and this was the last scheduled run that could act before it expires — so the correct move is to leave it alone. Nothing on the board beats Gomis on points per euro, no sale is legal while the squad sits at exactly eleven, and the flip mechanism is measurably absent. The one instruction that matters: do not add a second bid. After the Gomis commitment the remaining headroom is smaller than every other asset on the board, so a second winning bid would open a leveraged position, and a negative balance at matchday start scores zero for the entire matchday. The next run fires essentially at the expiry and is a resolving run, not a bidding run.

sell.reason: Nothing is sellable this run, and that is a hard constraint rather than a judgement call: at exactly eleven players any sale breaks the formation and forfeits the matchday. The three designated funding sales all stay on hold until the squad reaches twelve. Widmer remains the weakest link in the fielded eleven and his value is falling fastest; Bernardo carries an unchanged non-fit flag and was hooked at half time on the opening matchday for his direct competitor; Lokonga is a quality sale rather than an availability one and his value is drifting down. If Gomis lands, one sale becomes legal — but none is needed, because the buy does not require funding.

buy.reason: One live bid, already placed, and it is the whole buy list. Gomis is a Leipzig attacker with a confirmed start record this season, verified fit on a dated source naming him in the starting eleven, not on his club's injury list, and carrying the best points-per-euro figure on the board. He is bid comfortably clear of the highest clearing premium ever measured in this league, which is deliberate: the bid was sized against the high cluster, never the median, after two auctions were lost by bidding near the median. He is still the sole offer, but that means nothing — the Scheller rival appeared after twelve hours of being unopposed, so being alone on a listing is not evidence of anything. Everything else was rejected. The one new arrival is a defender with no points history at all, unaffordable if the live bid lands, and wrong for the shape. The best points-per-euro number on the board belongs to a defender carrying a non-fit flag — the classic cheap-value-next-to-a-big-average trap, and a future run must read the status field before being tempted by that ratio. Every manager ask on the board is priced far above where manager asks actually clear; a fresh manager-to-manager settlement this run landed right back in the low single digits, which is the third datapoint confirming that cluster. The fallback for a lost auction has been sharpened rather than reaffirmed: his big average was earned off a single start and a fraction of a full match, and no dated source from the last month confirms he is in the eleven, so his selection is unconfirmed rather than confirmed. He is still worth a high-cluster bid if the main auction is lost, and worth nothing at all if it is won.
